title: Python Programming — Basics to OOP
description: Complete Python course from the first program to object-oriented programming: syntax, data structures, functions, OOP, files, exceptions, NumPy and Pandas, with real-time examples and flow charts in every chapter.
objectives:
Write, run and debug Python programs from the command line and an editor
Use variables, data types, operators, input/output and type conversion correctly
Control program flow with all four forms of if, for and while loops, break, continue and loop-else
Choose and use strings, lists, tuples, sets and dictionaries, and write comprehensions
Write reusable functions, including closures, decorators, generators, lambdas and recursion
Organise code into modules and packages
Design programs with classes using encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism and abstraction
Read and write files and handle errors with exceptions
Analyse data with NumPy, Pandas and Matplotlib
outcomes:
Build complete console applications such as an ATM, shopping cart or login system
Explain mutable vs immutable types, scope and the four OOP pillars in interviews
Pick the right data structure for a problem and justify the choice
Model a real business problem with classes — the Employee Payroll System capstone
Load, clean, summarise and chart tabular data with Pandas and Matplotlib

modules.title: Unit 1 · Getting Started
modules.description: What Python is, how a program runs, setting up Python and the basic rules of the language.

lessons.title: 1. Introduction to Python
lessons.content:
Course notes: pages 3–4

Topics
• What is Python and why it is so widely used
• Interpreted, dynamically typed, platform independent, open source
• The huge standard library
• How a Python program actually runs (source → bytecode → interpreter)
• Where Python is used: web, data, automation, AI

lessons.title: 2. Installing Python & Writing Your First Program
lessons.content:
Course notes: pages 5–6

Topics
• Installing Python and checking the version
• Interactive shell vs running a .py file
• Choosing an editor or IDE — how and when to use each
• Writing, saving and running your first program

lessons.title: 3. Comments, Indentation, Keywords & Identifiers
lessons.content:
Course notes: pages 7–8

Topics
• Single-line and multi-line comments, docstrings
• Indentation — Python's most important rule
• Reserved keywords
• Identifiers — naming rules and case sensitivity
• Naming conventions for readable code

modules.title: Unit 2 · Data, Input/Output & Operators
modules.description: Variables and built-in types, converting between them, reading input, formatting output and every operator family.

lessons.title: 4. Variables and Data Types
lessons.content:
Course notes: pages 9–10

Topics
• Variables and dynamic typing
• int, float, complex, bool, str, None
• Mutable vs immutable — the concept interviewers love

lessons.title: 5. Type Conversion (Casting)
lessons.content:
Course notes: pages 11–12

Topics
• Implicit vs explicit conversion
• int(), float(), str(), bool(), list(), tuple(), set()

lessons.title: 6. Input and Output
lessons.content:
Course notes: pages 13–14

Topics
• Reading user input with input() and converting it

lessons.title: 7. Operators
lessons.content:
Course notes: pages 15–18

Topics
• Arithmetic, comparison, logical, assignment operators
• Identity, membership and bitwise operators
• Operator precedence

Practice programs
• Swap two numbers • Even or odd • Last digit of a number

• Seconds to hours, minutes, seconds • Split a bill among friends

modules.title: Unit 3 · Control Flow
modules.description: Making decisions and repeating work: all forms of if, for and while loops, and loop control statements.

lessons.title: 8. Conditional Statements — if / elif / else
lessons.content:
Course notes: pages 19–34

Topics
• Form 1 — the simple if
• Form 2 — if ... else
• Form 3 — if ... elif ... else (the ladder)
• Form 4 — nested if
• The one-line if (ternary operator)
• Truthy and falsy values
• match ... case (Python 3.10+)
• Common mistakes and a comparison of all four forms

Practice programs
• Largest of three numbers • Leap year • Voting eligibility
• Positive, negative or zero • Discount slab • Traffic signal
• Simple login check • BMI category

lessons.title: 9. for Loop

Course notes: pages 35–40

Practice programs

lessons.title: 10. while Loop

Course notes: pages 41–48

Practice programs

Course notes: pages 49–52

Topics

• continue — skip to the next iteration

Practice programs

• Print only even numbers • Stop reading marks at -1
